data.text: [00:03.9]So, erm … Valentine’s Day started hundreds of years ago. `[00:12.4]There was an emperor in Italy … and, well, … the emperor didn’t want his soldiers to get married … because he wanted the soldiers only to fight. `[00:24]But, a priest called Valentine helped soldiers to get married secretly. `[00:30]The emperor was angry about that and … he killed Valentine … on the fourteenth of February. `[00:37.9]So, now people celebrate love and romance on that day … in memory of Valentine.

[00:45.9]So, Valentine’s Day is on the fourteenth of February and people celebrate all over the world. `[00:53]Traditionally, people send cards to each other. `[00:56.8]And they give presents – flowers and chocolates, usually. `[01:01]And of course, it is traditional for a boyfriend to take his girlfriend out for a romantic dinner in a restaurant. `[01:10]It’s also a popular date for getting married.

[01:014.9]Some people think that Valentine’s Day is too commercial. `[01:19]They think that people buy too many cards and presents … but I don’t agree. `[01:25]I mean, people buy things of course, but I think it’s really good to celebrate love and romance.
